This is a data-integrity regression for the dedup/merge path.

findings.title: Removal of the max_segment_spans flush-time guard leaves only destructive in-insert eviction to bound segment size
findings.body: The diff removes the block in `_load_segment_data` that checked `if len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans:` and skipped the segment with `metrics.incr("spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded")` and an error log. The constructor still accepts `max_segment_spans: int = 1001` (line 150) and stores it (line 158), but it is now completely unused — dead configuration. Previously, an oversized segment was detected at flush time and *skipped* (with a metric), preserving the invariant that emitted segments never exceed the span limit. Now the only enforcement is the Lua script's `zpopmin` eviction during insert, which silently truncates the segment (see the add-buffer.lua finding). The safety net that turned a data-integrity problem into a visible, measurable error has been removed while its configuration knob remains, which is misleading. Either restore the flush-time check (as a defense in depth) or remove the now-unused `max_segment_spans` parameter and document that eviction is the sole mechanism.

findings.title: __reduce__ drops segment_page_size, max_segment_bytes, and max_segment_spans when pickling SpansBuffer
findings.body: `__reduce__` returns `(SpansBuffer, (self.assigned_shards, self.span_buffer_timeout_secs, self.span_buffer_root_timeout_secs, self.redis_ttl))` — it omits `segment_page_size`, `max_segment_bytes`, and `max_segment_spans`. The factory (src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py) uses `run_task_with_multiprocessing(partial(process_batch, buffer), ...)`, which pickles the buffer to worker processes. Any non-default values for those three parameters are silently reset to defaults (100, 10 MiB, 1001) in workers. This was already the case for the first two before this PR, but the PR makes `max_segment_spans` newly dead (see related finding), compounding the confusion. The pickle round-trip should include all constructor parameters that affect behavior.

findings.title: process_batch assumes end_timestamp_precise is always present in the span payload
findings.body: `end_timestamp_precise=val["end_timestamp_precise"]` uses direct key access on the parsed SpanEvent. The schema type `SpanEvent` (sentry_kafka_schemas.schema_types.ingest_spans_v1) may mark this field optional, and Relay/older producers may omit it; a missing key raises `KeyError`, which would fail the entire batch in `process_batch` and, because offsets are only committed after successful processing (CommitOffsets is downstream of the flusher), cause the consumer to retry the batch indefinitely — a poison-pill that stalls the spans consumer partition. The neighboring fields use `.get()` with defaults (`val.get("parent_span_id")`, `val.get("is_remote")`), showing the codebase's convention for optional fields. Use `val.get("end_timestamp_precise") or <fallback>` (e.g. the message timestamp already computed as `timestamp`) or validate the schema. The test payloads all include the field, so this path is untested for absence.

findings.title: Comment claims Cursor offsets may be negative, but no validation or handling exists and other paginators reject them
findings.body: The added comment 'Performance optimization: Allow negative offsets for advanced pagination scenarios' on `self.offset = int(offset)` implies the Cursor class now supports or handles negative offsets. In reality the class does nothing special — it just stores the int — and every paginator that consumes cursors either crashes on negative offsets (Django negative slicing, per the paginator.py findings) or explicitly rejects them with BadPaginationError. The comment documents an intention that the code does not implement and that the rest of the pagination stack contradicts; it will mislead maintainers into thinking negative offsets are a supported, safe feature.

findings.title: Pre-existing typo queryset.query.order_b (missing _by) in BasePaginator.build_queryset
findings.body: Line 105 reads `queryset.query.order_b = tuple(new_order_by)` — the attribute is `order_by`, so this silently sets a new, meaningless attribute and leaves the ordering unchanged. This is a pre-existing bug (not introduced by this PR), but it sits directly in the code path that the new OptimizedCursorPaginator inherits and that the modified `get_result` exercises for prev-cursors on already-ordered querysets, so the PR's changes interact with it: when a prev cursor is used on a queryset already ordered by `-key`, the intended order reversal never happens. Worth fixing while touching this file, since the PR's stated goal is correct bidirectional pagination.

findings.title: No test covers the new 1000-span eviction path in add-buffer.lua
findings.body: The PR adds eviction logic (`if span_count > 1000 then zpopmin ...`) to the Lua script and removes the flush-time `max_segment_spans` guard, but tests/sentry/spans/test_buffer.py contains no test that ingests more than 1000 spans into a single segment and asserts which spans survive eviction or that the segment remains complete/consistent. All existing tests use 4-5 spans per trace. Given that eviction drops the lowest-scored (earliest end_timestamp) members — potentially including the segment root — the behavior of the eviction path (which spans are dropped, whether the hrs flag stays consistent, whether flushed output is a truncated segment) is completely unverified. A test should ingest >1000 spans with distinct end_timestamp_precise values and assert the surviving set and the emitted segment contents.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates ~70 lines of BasePaginator.get_result instead of overriding a hook
findings.body: The new class copies the entire `get_result` body from `BasePaginator` (lines 136-215) and adds one conditional branch for negative offsets. Any future fix to the shared logic (e.g. the `order_b` typo, cursor trimming edge cases, hits handling) must be applied in two places or the paginators diverge. The negative-offset behavior could be a small override or a parameter on BasePaginator. As a standalone duplication it is a maintenance hazard rather than an immediate bug, but it already diverges: the copy retains the `max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` line from the modified base, so the two implementations will drift as the base evolves.
